summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara studied at Wat Bowonniwet Vihara and under Satyananda Puri and Vajirayanavangsa. He served as abbot of Wat Bowonniwet Vihara (~1961–2013) and held posts at Mahamakut Buddhist University (1961) and Kasetsart University (1976).

Sonam Chhoki works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. She completed an M.A. at Jawaharlal Nehru University and a Ph.D. at SOAS University of London, and she has served as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.

Sonam Choden works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, she has been a Doctoral Local Researcher and a project researcher (Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin) at the University of Hamburg.

A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Sonam Gyatso was a research assistant at Toyo Bunko around 1961 and served as a professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014). He taught Shinjo Kawasaki and Chogye Shabdrung.

Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Sonam Jamtsho studied as a Doctoral Local Researcher and served as a project researcher (Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter) at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026). He also taught Gembo Dorji.

Sonam Kachru specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, earning a PhD from the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold. He held fellowships at Forum Transregionale Studien and MPIWG, and became Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Yale University (attested 2026).

Sonam Thakchoe is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania (~1999–2002) mentored by Jay L. Garfield and Jeff Malpas. He held a post at the University of Tasmania around 2003.

Sonam Tsering works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, having studied under doctoral supervisor Gray Tuttle and several other teachers. Attested in 2026, he is Senior Lecturer in Tibetan and Director of the Tibetan Language Program at Columbia University.

Sondra L. Hausner is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. Attested in 2026, she holds appointments as Professor of Anthropology of Religion at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford.
Working in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Songeun Choe studied under MA supervisor Myung-dae Moon and under doctoral supervisor Kiyohiko Munakata (attested 1991).

Sonja Arntzen is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of British Columbia (~1970–1979) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz (~1972–1979), as well as under Seizan Yanagida and Sojo Hirano.

A linguist who completed her degrees and habilitation at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1986–2005), Sonja Glauch held posts at Heidelberg University Library (1998–1999), Erlangen-Nuremberg (2007), University of Vienna (2008), and University of Munich (2009–2010).

Sonya S. Lee works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. She earned her PhD from the University of Chicago under Hung Wu (attested 2004) and held posts at Swarthmore College (2003–2004), Stanford University, and the University of Southern California (attested 2010).

Soon-il Hwang specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA at Dongguk University under Seung-won Seo and a DPhil at Mansfield College, Oxford, supervised by Richard Gombrich, later holding a post at Dongguk University.

Working in Buddhist studies and religious studies, Soorakkulame Pemaratana studied at the National University of Singapore under thesis supervisor Saranindranath Tagore. Attested in 2026, he serves as Visiting Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Sophus Bugge was a linguist who studied at the universities of Oslo (~1851–1857), Copenhagen (~1857–1858), and Berlin (~1858–1859), and under Albrecht Weber (1858). In 1866, he became Professor of Comparative Linguistics and Old Norse at the University of Oslo.
Soshu Nishioka is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Shitennoji University, with his tenure attested in 2000 and 2015.

Soshuku Shibatani specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and Koyasan University (master's 2003–2007; doctorate ~2008–2013), and held posts at Sonoda Women's University, the Society for the Study of Pilgrimage, and Koyasan University.

Sotan Oka worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studying under Bokusan Nishiari, Teizo Shiratori, and Fusho Nagano. He was a professor and dean (1899) and president (1918) at Komazawa University, and founded Antai-ji in 1921.

Soyen Shaku was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Keio University (1885–1887) and under Kosen Imakita, among others. He was a Zen master at Engaku-ji (1892) and served as president of Hanazono University (1914–1917).
